COMPANY
De La Rue

Basingstoke, United Kingdom

De La Rue is a banknote printer based in Basingstoke, United Kingdom, tied to eight central banks. It prints notes for the Bank of England (a 500 million pound contract decided 29 September 2014, extended to 2028), Kenya, Sweden, Libya, South Sudan, Tanzania and, per a trial witness, historically for Nigeria. In South Sudan, a UN report said it sent about 1.4 million dollars between 2016 and September 2017 to a Nairobi account held by a Bank of South Sudan consultant, against a contract worth about 144 million dollars, and noted 'suspected corruption'. The UK Serious Fraud Office opened an investigation in July 2019 and closed it in June 2020 without charges. In September 2010 De La Rue said some employees had falsified banknote paper test certificates, followed by a supply suspension to the Reserve Bank of India.

Source says: Bank of South Sudan (South Sudan). De La Rue paid or bribed officials of the Bank of South Sudan (South Sudan). A UN Human Rights Council commission report said De La Rue transferred about $1.4 million to an Equity Bank account in Nairobi held by a Bank of South Sudan consultant between 2016 and September 2017, against a banknote contract worth about $144 million, and noted 'suspected corruption'. The UK Serious Fraud Office closed its own investigation in June 2020 without charges. Kenyan bank link in South Sudan bribery (Daily Nation)

Source says: Bank of South Sudan (South Sudan). De La Rue is named in a bribery or misconduct case involving the Bank of South Sudan (South Sudan). The UK Serious Fraud Office opened an investigation into De La Rue in July 2019 over suspected corruption in South Sudan (South Sudan awarded it a 2011 contract for 2.8 billion banknotes) and closed it in June 2020, saying the case did not meet the test for prosecution. City A.M.: SFO ends corruption probe into banknote printer De La Rue

Source says: Reserve Bank of India (India). De La Rue is named in a bribery or misconduct case involving the Reserve Bank of India (India). De La Rue said in September 2010 that some employees had deliberately falsified banknote paper specification test certificates for a limited number of customers; Eye Radio reports this was followed by suspension of supply to the Reserve Bank of India (customer link per Eye Radio). Central Banking: De La Rue says staff falsified banknote tests; Eye Radio (2020)

Source says: Bank of England (United Kingdom). De La Rue prints banknotes for the Bank of England (United Kingdom). Bank of England awarded De La Rue PLC the 'Banknote Print' contract (decision 29 September 2014, value £500,000,000) to print Bank of England notes at the Bank's Debden site in Essex. Find a Tender notice 013490-2024: Bank of England Banknote Print

Source says: Bank of England (United Kingdom). De La Rue prints banknotes for the Bank of England (United Kingdom). The Bank of England triggered a three-year extension of its polymer banknote contract with De La Rue, which had been due to end in 2025 (to 2028); notes printed at the Bank's Debden facility. LBC: Bank of England extends polymer banknote contract to 2028

Source says: Central Bank of Kenya (Kenya). De La Rue prints banknotes for the Central Bank of Kenya (Kenya). The Central Bank of Kenya awarded the contract to print new-look currency (Sh18 billion) to De La Rue International, which operates the Ruaraka plant co-owned by the Kenyan government; De La Rue beat Giesecke & Devrient, Crane Currency and Oberthur Fiduciaire. Crane AB disputed the award before the procurement review board. Business Daily Africa: CBK defends De La Rue new currency contract

Source says: Sveriges Riksbank (Sweden). De La Rue prints banknotes for Sveriges Riksbank (Sweden). Sveriges Riksbank signed an agreement with De La Rue (announced 19 September 2018) to print Swedish banknotes for just over three years, replacing Crane. Central Banking: De La Rue beats European competition to Swedish banknote contract

Source says: Central Bank of Libya (Libya). De La Rue prints banknotes for the Central Bank of Libya (Libya). The MEI article states that the regular Libyan dinar notes are printed by Britain's De La Rue. Middle East Institute (Jonathan M. Winer): Seized Russian-printed dinars...

Source says: Bank of South Sudan (South Sudan). De La Rue prints banknotes for the Bank of South Sudan (South Sudan). South Sudan awarded De La Rue a contract to produce 2.8 billion banknotes in 2011, and new notes including 500-pound notes were printed by De La Rue in 2019. Eye Radio: Case dropped against S.Sudan banknotes, passports printing firm

Source says: Central Bank of Nigeria (Nigeria). De La Rue has another documented tie to the Central Bank of Nigeria (Nigeria). At the EFCC trial of former CBN Governor Godwin Emefiele over alleged unlawful printing of redesigned naira notes (2022), a prosecution witness said original naira designs were historically handled by De La Rue, while the new notes were printed locally. BusinessDay: Witness alleges Emefiele breached CBN Act in naira redesign trial

Source says: Bank of Tanzania (Tanzania). De La Rue prints banknotes for the Bank of Tanzania (Tanzania). De La Rue International Limited was one of two companies that won the Bank of Tanzania's tender to reprint Sh10,000, Sh5,000, Sh2,000 and Sh1,000 notes, reported 28 May 2024. Why two companies won Bank of Tanzania banknote reprint tender (The Citizen)

Source says: Bank of Ghana (Ghana). De La Rue prints banknotes for the Bank of Ghana (Ghana). In a report on the Bank of Ghana's upgraded cedi notes signed on 4 March 2019 and announced on 8 April 2019, retired Bank of Ghana Deputy Governor Emmanuel Asiedu-Mante states that the cedi is printed by De La Rue, a security printing firm based in the United Kingdom, and that the printer charges in British pounds. No contract value is given. See the company that prints the Ghana Cedi notes (Daily Graphic / Graphic Online)

Source says: Danmarks Nationalbank (Denmark). De La Rue prints banknotes for Danmarks Nationalbank (Denmark). Danmarks Nationalbank has signed an agreement with De La Rue to produce Denmark's new banknote series at De La Rue's facility outside London; the notes are due for launch in 2028 and the contract runs for a minimum of six years with an option to extend. No value is stated. De La Rue Wins Contract to Print Denmark's New Series (Currency News)

Source says: ECCB. De La Rue supplies banknote material for ECCB. De La Rue states that the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank's EC$2 commemorative polymer banknote is designed on De La Rue's SAFEGUARD polymer substrate and joins the all-polymer ECCB series first introduced in 2019; ECCB Governor Timothy Antoine is quoted saying 'in De La Rue, we have a partner on whom we can rely.' The release does not say who printed the note. De La Rue: Eastern Caribbean Central Bank Unveils Innovative $2 Polymer Banknote (De La Rue plc, via MarketScreener)

Source says: National Bank of Ethiopia (Ethiopia). De La Rue prints banknotes for the National Bank of Ethiopia (Ethiopia). Addis Fortune reports that the National Bank of Ethiopia awarded De La Rue of the United Kingdom a 187 million Br share of a 206 million Br banknote printing deal, covering the 100 Br note. Two Overseas Firms Seal Deal to Print Banknotes (Addis Fortune)

An interview with the Bank of Mauritius published on the Bank's own website (a Currency News special issue for the Banknote 2014 conference) refers to "the Rs500 note supplied by De La Rue". The document says "supplied by" rather than "printed by", and gives no contract value and no indication of the position after 2014. Putting the 'Swing' into the New Mauritius Notes (Bank of Mauritius communique)

Source says: Bank of Albania (Albania). De La Rue prints banknotes for the Bank of Albania (Albania). A De La Rue press release headed "The Bank of Albania launches new polymer banknote series, originated and printed by De La Rue" states that the series was "originated and produced by De La Rue", covering the 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000 leke denominations, with the 200 and 5000 leke entering circulation "from 30 September" and the rest over the following three years. No year and no contract value are given on the page. The Bank of Albania launches new polymer banknote series, originated and printed by De La Rue (press release)

The statement covers that denomination only; the announcement says nothing about who prints Iceland's other notes. New 10,000 kr. banknote in circulation

Source says: Reserve Bank of Fiji (Fiji). De La Rue: prints some of its banknotes (the Reserve Bank of Fiji (Fiji)). A Reserve Bank of Fiji press release states that the bank 'signed an agreement for the printing of a series of new design Fiji banknotes with De La Rue International Limited' of the United Kingdom, and that a $100 note would be introduced for the first time. The release does not list the other denominations or the contract value. Press Release No. 01/2006 - Printing of Fiji's New Currency Notes

Securamonde reports on the Central Bank of Seychelles' new banknote family and states that the banknotes were 'printed by UK banknote printers De La Rue'. No contract value, volume or term is given. Seychelles issues new banknote family

Source says: National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia (North Macedonia). De La Rue: prints some of its banknotes (the National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia (North Macedonia)). The National Bank concluded three contracts with De La Rue International Ltd to print new 10, 500 and 1,000 denar banknotes, 45 million notes in all, for a total of 3.775 million euros. Maldives Launches New Family of Polymer Banknotes (De La Rue press release)

Source says: Bermuda Monetary Authority (Bermuda). De La Rue prints banknotes for Bermuda Monetary Authority (Bermuda). The Bermuda Monetary Authority's press release of 30 October 2024 announces that the new $2 and $5 banknotes printed by De La Rue on SAFEGUARD polymer substrate will enter circulation that autumn, Bermuda's first polymer notes and among the first to carry King Charles III's effigy; De La Rue's currency managing director Ruth Euling says it was a privilege to design and deliver them. Bermuda Monetary Authority Releases New $2 and $5 Banknotes Printed on Polymer

BanknoteNews records the printer of Turkmenistan's commemorative 200-manat note (B243a), introduced 1 December 2025 for the 30th anniversary of permanent neutrality, as De La Rue; the note is 150 x 75 mm on Safeguard polymer with a holographic stripe showing the Arkadag monument in PureImage. INTERNATIONAL BODY
International Monetary Fund

Washington, United States

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is an international lender based in Washington, United States, tied to 16 central banks and one other party. Its former staff have gone on to lead central banks. Kamau Thugge went from IMF staff to governor of the Central Bank of Kenya, and Reza Baqir from IMF staff to governor of the State Bank of Pakistan. Agustín Carstens went from IMF deputy managing director to governor of the Bank of Mexico, and Raghuram Rajan from IMF chief economist to governor of the Reserve Bank of India. Ahsan H Mansur went from IMF staff to governor of Bangladesh Bank. These are career moves, not accusations. The IMF also appears in cases. In May 2023 Argentina's central bank used 99.2% of a transfer limit it had agreed with the IMF. In December 2021 Malawi police arrested Kabambe and Mwanamvekha, saying they falsified figures to make the IMF believe Malawi met loan conditions. In March 2008 the IMF Executive Board found that the National Bank of Tajikistan had supplied inaccurate information, including reporting reserves of about $450 million when they were roughly one-third of that, and Tajikistan was required to repay $47.4 million. The IMF also sits on the Financial Stability Board.

Source says: BCEAO. The Bank for International Settlements holds gold reserves belonging to BCEAO. Note 6 of the BCEAO's financial statements for 2024 lists the Bank for International Settlements as one of the three places its gold is held, alongside its own head office and the Banque de France. Agence Ecofin, reading the statements, puts the BIS holding at close to 106,000 ounces valued at 176.4 billion CFA francs, and says it fell during 2024 as part of the gold was redeployed into placement operations; about 200,000 ounces were in such operations at the end of 2024, adding 37 billion CFA francs to the year's revaluation. Source says: BCEAO. The Bank for International Settlements manages reserves or funds for BCEAO. The BCEAO's own audited accounts for 2025 say it has bought units in an investment fund called BISIP K, and that the fund is managed by the Bank for International Settlements ("La BCEAO a souscrit a des parts du Fonds Commun de Placement denomme BISIP K, gerees par la Banque des Reglements Internationaux (BRI)"). The BISIP K units were worth 205,811 million FCFA on 31 December 2025, down from 222,297 million FCFA a year earlier. The accounts group these units with the bank's holdings kept for immediate liquidity. BCEAO - Etats financiers de la BCEAO au 31 decembre 2025 (Note 8, Parts de fonds commun de placement)

Source says: Bank of Japan (Japan). The Bank for International Settlements holds gold reserves belonging to the Bank of Japan (Japan). A Bank of Japan statistics notice explains that the Bank's gold claims on the Bank for International Settlements were moved out of a "Gold Sight Account" and into a "Gold Ear-marked Account" with the BIS, an ear-marked account being gold held for the depositor. The notice says "The Bank of Japan opened its sight account by paying US dollar cash and the BIS purchased gold using the cash", that "Sight account holders can withdraw the equivalent amount of gold anytime", and that "the claims are now booked as 'gold' together with the existing gold holdings by the Bank." It calls the change technical, with no new gold bought. The notice dates from 2000 and covers only this portion of the holding; the Bank of Japan does not say where its other gold sits. Bank of Japan - Notice on the Bank of Japan Accounts: gold (statistics outline)

Source says: Central Bank of the Argentine Republic (Argentina). The Bank for International Settlements holds gold reserves belonging to the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic (Argentina). The governor of Argentina's central bank, Santiago Bausili, told the Senate that part of the BCRA's gold is deposited at the Bank for International Settlements in Switzerland. As reported, he said the gold "esta depositada en el Banco de Pagos Internacionales (BIS, por sus siglas en ingles), en Suiza", and described the decision as "depositar una parte de las reservas en lingotes en el BIS." He attached no tonnage to the location; a BCRA reserves report of late May 2026 puts the whole holding at "1,98 millones de oro fino en onzas troy, cerca de 61 toneladas". El Banco Central confirmo que una parte del oro esta en Suiza (Chequeado)
